study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Wu and Baeken, Journal of Affective Disorders, 2023
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Normative modeling analysis reveals corpus callosum volume changes in early and mid-to-late first episode major depression

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) implemented in the PCNToolkit (v.0.18) to train normative models on healthy participants. This approach was employed to accommodate inter-site variation across 7 study sites.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: To accommodate inter-site variation, hierarchical Bayesian regression was employed to train the normative models on healthy participants (Rutherford et al., 2022).

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The response variable was the volume of the Corpus Callosum (CC) and its subvolumes (genu, body, splenium). These are white matter volumes measured using VBM and parcellated based on the JHU DTI-based white-matter atlases.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Besides the entire CC, based on the JHU DTI-based white-matter atlases, the CC was further anatomically divided in the genu, body, and splenium

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Gender, age, education, and total intracranial volume were used as fixed effects covariates. Site was included as a hierarchical effect to accommodate inter-site variation via hierarchical Bayesian regression.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: we fitted normative models using gender, age, education, and total intracranial volume as fixed effects covariates to predict CC (sub)volumes. ... To accommodate inter-site variation, hierarchical Bayesian regression was employed
